summaryEn: Teaches you to talk about the past, telling the two perfect auxiliaries apart.
Teaches you the irregular participles of common verbs and why they have to be learnt by heart.
Teaches you the participle of separable verbs: the syllable that slips in between prefix and stem.
Teaches you to tell an evening in order: first, then, and last of all.
Teaches you to describe a morning that went wrong: the delay, the missed train, the mishap.
Teaches you to talk about your childhood, using the past of 'to be' and 'to have'.
Teaches you to compare the past with today: there was, there wasn't, it was different.
Teaches you to describe something you did for the first time and how it felt.
Teaches you to sum up the past week: what you got done and what happened.
Teaches you to share good news and to surprise the person you are talking to.
Teaches you to tell a life story in order: how old you were and what happened next.
Teaches you to talk about a past wish, about what you could not do and what you had to do.
Teaches you to say what was compulsory and what was forbidden at school, in the past tense.
Teaches you to tell the story of a move from start to finish and to say how hard it was at first.
Teaches you to tell the story of meeting someone and of a relationship, using reflexive verbs.
Teaches you to tell a stretch of time that is still running from a point left in the past.
Teaches you to say what has changed and what you have got used to.
Teaches you to tell childhood memories: what it was like there, what there was, what was allowed.
Teaches you to tell an embarrassing thing that happened to you.
Teaches you to talk about something you achieved and the work behind it.
Teaches you to take and give advice, with three patterns built on the modal 'sollen'.
Teaches you to say how you feel and introduces the little pronoun that reflexive verbs carry.
Teaches you to ask permission, understand a ban and tell three modal verbs apart.
Teaches you to give gentle advice and to talk about home remedies.
Teaches you to ask about the dose, the side effects and whether a prescription is needed.
Teaches you to describe an injury and the pattern German uses to say what you hurt.
Teaches you to understand and answer the insurance questions asked at a practice reception.
Teaches you to describe an urgent toothache on the phone and to confirm the instructions given.
Teaches you to talk about stress and where the reflexive pronoun sits in a negative sentence.
Teaches you to discuss regular health checks and to phrase advice that holds for everyone.
Teaches you to name the person correctly when you give something to someone.
Teaches you to ask who something belongs to and to answer.
Teaches you to say where something stands and to pick the right verb.
Teaches you to pick the right form and verb when you put something somewhere.
Teaches you to furnish a room together and to argue about where things go.
Teaches you to describe what is where in your neighbourhood.
Teaches you to ask a neighbour for help and for things, and to thank them.
Teaches you to accept a parcel for a neighbour and to hand it over.
Teaches you to raise the noise from upstairs politely and to soften the complaint.
Teaches you to describe a fault at home and to arrange an appointment for the repair.
Teaches you to talk about looking for work and starting a new job.
Teaches you the subordinate clause of reason and why the verb moves to the end.
Teaches you the conjunction of reason that leaves the verb in place, and how it differs from the other.
Teaches you to introduce yourself and someone else at work.
Teaches you to give an opinion in a meeting and to build a subordinate clause with 'dass'.
Teaches you to answer the phone at work, take a note and pass a message on.
Teaches you to state a preference at lunch and to choose a dish.
Teaches you to make a request for leave in writing and in person.
Teaches you to report an illness to work and to send the sick note by email.
Teaches you to understand and respond to feedback in an appraisal.
